d: Preparation of very finely ground coffee boiled unfiltered in a cezve, inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.
tech: slow heating of coffee and water in a long-handled pot until it foams, served with grounds settling
mat: hammered copper or brass, tinned; silver; later steel and ceramic
auth: hand-hammered marks, tinned interior, riveted long handle; capacity sized in cups

d: Japanese vegetable pickling in salt, brine or a fermented rice-bran bed, using tubs, pressing stones and screw-top pickle presses.
tech: Vegetables pressed under weight in salt or buried in a daily-stirred rice-bran (nuka) bed.
mat: Wooden or ceramic tubs, enamel or plastic nukadoko containers, pickle presses
auth: Traditional nukadoko is kept alive by daily hand-stirring; pressing containers are judged by lid pressure and capacity rather than brand.

d: Hard white charcoal from ubame oak, prized for long, clean, hot burning in Japanese grilling.
tech: Slow kiln pyrolysis (about 240 °C for 120 hours), then about 1,000 °C, cured in damp earth, sand and ash
auth: Wakayama Prefectural Charcoal Cooperative yellow label; regional collective trademark since 2006; metallic ring when struck

r: Rhubarb Triangle, West Yorkshire, England (Wakefield, Morley, Rothwell)
d: Rhubarb crowns grown two years in the field, then forced in heated dark sheds and picked by candlelight.
tech: field-grown roots frosted, moved into heated windowless sheds in November, harvested by candlelight
auth: 'Yorkshire Forced Rhubarb' carries EU Protected Designation of Origin (2010).

d: Seed-koji merchants who keep, cultivate and sell koji mould spores to sake, miso and soy-sauce makers.
tech: koji mould grown on steamed rice with wood ash, spores sold on grain or as powder
mat: Aspergillus oryzae and related moulds; rice, barley
auth: about ten moyashiya remain in Japan; strains are chosen per product (sake, miso, shōchū)

d: Fermented milk made with kefir grains, traditionally in goatskin bags hung by the door.
tech: grains added to milk, strained and reused; grains enlarge and split
mat: cow, goat or sheep milk; kefir grains
auth: true kefir is made from grains; powdered starters do not form grains

d: Mesophilic ropy fermented milks set at room temperature.
tech: mesophilic lactic fermentation with surface Geotrichum candidum
auth: long, ropy texture and velvety mould surface

r: Western Norway (Hordaland, Sogn og Fjordane, Møre og Romsdal)
d: Farm brewing of juniper-infused ale with each farm's own kveik yeast, passed down in families.
tech: juniper infusion, long boil or raw ale, warm fermentation of about 48 hours
auth: kveik kept on yeast rings, wooden logs or as dried flakes; strains named for farm or brewer

d: Hand rolling of premium cigars by torcedores from tobacco grown in the Vuelta Abajo.
tech: Hand rolling (totalmente a mano) by torcedores, mostly women today
mat: Tobacco from Vuelta Abajo and Semi Vuelta, Pinar del Río
auth: Boxes and labels carry 'Hecho en Cuba'; 'Totalmente a mano' marks fully handmade cigars.

d: Clove-and-tobacco cigarettes first made in Kudus, credited to Hajj Djamhari, first sold as medicine.
tech: Tobacco blended with minced dried clove buds, hand-rolled or machine-made
auth: Crackling sound when burning; sold by named Indonesian makers.

d: Moist steam-pasteurised tobacco placed under the upper lip, shifting from nasal snuff to snus by the early 1800s.
tech: Steam pasteurisation rather than fermentation; loose or portion
auth: Sold in Sweden under the EU exemption; most other EU sales of tobacco snus are banned.

d: Water-pipe smoking of sweetened muʽassel tobacco, called shisha in Egypt and arjīlah in the Levant.
tech: Molasses-fermented tobacco smoked over charcoal
auth: Sealed packs from named makers such as Al Fakher and Nakhla.

d: Turkish water pipe tradition, nargile.
tech: Water pipe smoking

d: Persian water pipe, with literary reference by Ahlī Shirazi before 1535 and a court post of hookah tender.
tech: Water pipe smoking
mat: Glass and precious metals for the rich

d: Italian meat products, mostly cured pork, served as antipasto; the name comes from Latin sal, salt.
tech: Salting and curing; some, such as mortadella, are cooked.
auth: Some are PDO (prosciutto di Parma, San Daniele); others such as Salame Felino hold the Italian traditional agri-food product (PAT) status.

d: Raw dry-cured hind leg made under EU protected designation of origin in two named zones.
tech: Salted in stages, rested, then hung in humidity-controlled rooms; aged at least 14 months.
mat: Pig hind leg and sea salt only; no nitrites or nitrates for Parma.
auth: Consorzio del Prosciutto di Parma brands each ham with the ducal crown after a horse-bone needle check; the word prosciutto alone is not protected.

r: Spain and Portugal (Huelva, Córdoba, Cáceres, Badajoz, Salamanca, Alentejo)
d: Dry-curing of hind legs from black Iberian pigs reared on dehesa oak pasture.
tech: Final fattening on acorns and grass; cured for months to years.
auth: Four PDOs; since 2014 coloured labels: black (100% ibérico de bellota, the only pata negra), red, green and white.

d: Stuffed and cured sausages; the Royal Spanish Academy defines embutido as intestine stuffed with minced meat, mainly pork.
tech: Stuffing into casings, then curing.
mat: Pork, sometimes blood and other fillings.

d: Branch of French cuisine devoted to prepared meat products, mainly pork: ham, sausage, terrines, confit.
tech: Salt-curing and brining, forcemeats, fermentation.

d: Sausage-making with more than 1,500 types, mostly in natural casings, with strict composition rules since the 13th century.
tech: Raw, cooked and smoked sausage making.

d: Regional sausages smoked or fresh, of pork, beef, veal or turkey, with dozens of varieties.
tech: Smoking, air-drying, scalding.
auth: EU PGI for kiełbasa lisiecka, kiełbasa biała parzona wielkopolska and kiełbasa piaszczańska; TSG for kabanosy staropolskie, krakowska sucha staropolska and others.

d: Wind-dried and cured pork and duck eaten with rice, especially in autumn and winter.
tech: Marinating in soy, Shaoxing wine and spices, then hanging to dry.
mat: Pork belly, pork and fat, duck.

d: Local chickens whose parents, or one parent, are native to Japan, raised by a prescribed method.
tech: Slow rearing at low stocking density.

d: Finishing oysters in shallow clay ponds left from old salt marshes, where Blue Navicula algae colours the gills green.
tech: affinage in claires, 28 days up to 8 months
mat: clay ponds, tidal fresh and salt water
auth: PGI and Label Rouge labels

r: Cantabria and the Basque Country, Spain
d: Hand-processed canning of bonito del norte and anchovies on the Bay of Biscay coast, in oil or escabeche.
tech: loins cooked in salt water, cleaned by hand, packed in olive oil or escabeche and sterilised in an autoclave
auth: check the can names Thunnus alalunga, not atún claro

d: Hand-prepared tinned sardines, tuna and mackerel in olive oil, with aged vintage tins valued like wine.
tech: fish cut and gutted by hand, steamed outside the can, packed in tinplate and aged at least six months
mat: sardines, tuna, carapau, cod, octopus, olive oil, tinplate
auth: look for aged reserve tins and ANICP member producers

d: Baltic sprats smoked on alder and canned in oil under a producers' logo.
tech: alder smoking then canning in oil
auth: the Riga Sprats in Oil logo of the member association

d: Salt-curing of spring-caught Cantabrian anchovies for at least six months before filleting and packing in olive oil.
tech: clean, salt, cure six months or more, wash, fillet by hand, pack in olive oil
auth: fillets firm but flexible, 9 to 12 cm, only anchovies, olive oil and salt; kept chilled

r: Caspian and Black Sea, Iran and Russia
d: Salt-cured roe of wild beluga, ossetra and sevruga sturgeon, the traditional meaning of caviar, now replaced largely by farmed roe.
tech: ovaries removed, sieved, rinsed, salted malossol-style, graded and tinned
mat: beluga, ossetra and sevruga roe, salt
auth: CITES-labelled tins with species named

d: Caviar from sturgeon raised, farmed and slaughtered in France after wild Gironde fishing was banned.
tech: Siberian sturgeon farmed up to nine years, roe graded grain by grain and lightly salted
auth: Caviar d'Aquitaine collective trademark (2013), IGP in preparation

r: Portugal, with fish from Norway and Iceland
d: Dry-salted cod, a Portuguese staple adopted from Basque salting off Newfoundland.
tech: cod gutted, salted and air-dried
auth: TSG label Bacalhau de Cura Tradicional Portuguesa

d: Skrei hung to dry outdoors for about three months, Norway's oldest food export still traded.
tech: open-air racks, cold wind, then sorting into 20-plus grades
auth: Tørrfisk fra Lofoten PGI

d: Baltic herring brined then canned to ferment further, sold from the third Thursday of August.
tech: caught May and June, brined, headed and gutted, barrelled at 15 to 18 C, canned early July
auth: sale date and tin fermentation

d: Ghee made by culturing boiled milk into curd, churning out the butter and simmering it until the solids brown.
tech: milk set to curd (dahi), churned in a wooden bilona to separate makhan from chaas, butter slowly heated and strained
mat: cow or water-buffalo milk, curd starter
auth: ingredient list of milk or butter only; nutty, caramel aroma; cream-based ghee skips the curd step

d: Pastoral Pokot method of fermenting raw milk in smoked gourds and finishing it with tree ash.
tech: raw milk kept at least three days in gourds smoked over kromwo wood, whey drained, shaken, ash added
mat: goat's or cow's milk, gourd calabashes, kromwo (Ozoroa insignis) ash
auth: light grey colour and aromatic, resinous note from the ash

p: Ancient; kefir found in Bronze Age graves c. 3,600 years old
d: Grain-fermented milk of North Caucasian, notably Circassian, tradition that spread through the Soviet Union and worldwide.
tech: 2–5% kefir grains in milk for 12–24 hours at 20–25 °C, then strained and reused
mat: cow's, goat's or sheep's milk, traditionally raw
auth: Made with living kefir grains (bacteria and yeasts in a kefiran matrix), not only a powdered starter

d: Room-temperature fermented milks of the Nordic countries, from thick filmjölk to ropy viili and drinkable piimä.
tech: Mesophilic fermentation with Lactococcus lactis and Leuconostoc; Geotrichum candidum on viili
auth: Mesophilic cultures give a mild, buttery sourness; viili has a velvety mould surface

p: Described by Herodotus (5th century BC) and William of Rubruck (13th century)
d: Fermented mare's milk of Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Bashkir, Kalmyk, Mongol and Yakut peoples.
tech: Liquid starter of lactobacilli and yeasts; mildly alcoholic (0.7–2.5%)
auth: Made from mare's milk; industrial versions use cow's milk adjusted with sucrose or whey

d: Thick sour milk of Zulu, Xhosa, Ndebele, Swazi and Sotho tradition, eaten over maize porridge.
tech: Unpasteurised milk fermented one to five days in a smoked calabash or hide sack, whey drained
auth: Traditional amasi is calabash-fermented raw milk; commercial versions use Lactococcus lactis on pasteurised milk

p: Whey spreads for at least 2,500 years; firm cream brunost from 1863
d: Boiling whey, with milk or cream, until the milk sugars caramelise into brown whey cheese or spread.
tech: Whey reduced about 10:1 in iron pots; cream added for the firm modern cheese
mat: Cow's and goat's whey, milk and cream
auth: Ekte geitost contains no cow's milk; Gudbrandsdalsost mixes cow's and goat's milk

r: Swiss Alps, Jura massif, Savoie, Allgäu, Vorarlberg and Tyrol
d: Large cooked-pressed cheeses from raw cow's milk made in village co-operatives and summer Alp huts, then aged for months.
tech: curd cooked in copper cauldrons, sometimes over wood fire, pressed into large wheels, brined and cellar-aged with turning and brushing
mat: raw cow's milk from pasture or hay, no silage
auth: AOP/PDO marks, casein or rind marks, Comté green or brown band, Appenzeller colour labels

d: Farmhouse cheddar made from the farm's own raw milk, cheddared by hand, bound in cloth and aged at least a year.
tech: cheddaring by hand, cloth binding, long cellar ageing
mat: raw cow's milk, rennet, cloth, lard
auth: Raw milk, cloth-bound natural rind, maker's farm name; Slow Food presidium members.

d: Ripening of Lacaune ewe's-milk blue cheese in the natural Combalou caves, the only place where Roquefort may be aged.
tech: Cave ageing with Penicillium roqueforti
auth: Roquefort PDO name and aging in the Combalou caves.

d: Mountain blue cheeses of cow's or mixed milks matured in natural limestone caves and once wrapped in leaves.
tech: Natural cave ripening at about 90% humidity and 7–13 °C
mat: Raw cow's milk, often blended with goat and sheep milk
auth: PDO or PGI stamp on the wrapper; Cabrales in dark green foil.

d: Handmade raw-milk cheese made on Dutch farms from at least half the farm's own milk.
tech: Raw-milk pressed-curd cheesemaking on the farm, often with cumin or other seeds and herbs
mat: Raw cow's, goat's, sheep's or buffalo milk
auth: Boerenkaas TSG name; raw milk, at least half from the producing farm

d: Aged hard cheese with many small irregular holes, a style unique to Sweden.
tech: Curd salted in the mass rather than brined; long cellar ageing; waxed wheels
auth: Svecia PGI mark; made in Sweden from Swedish milk

r: Portugal and western Spain (Beira, Alentejo, Extremadura)
d: Raw ewe's-milk cheeses coagulated with cardoon (Cynara cardunculus) flowers instead of animal rennet, ripened to a soft paste.
tech: thistle-flower coagulation, slow draining, cloth binding
mat: raw sheep's milk, cardoon pistils, salt
auth: PDO label and regulatory council seal; raw milk; slightly bitter note from thistle

d: Farmhouse raw cow's-milk cheese of Portuguese origin, registered by IPHAN as Brazilian intangible heritage in 2008.
tech: raw milk, rennet and 'pingo' whey starter, hand pressing, open-air maturing
auth: Raw milk; regional geographical indication or registered producer

r: Cantal and Aubrac, Massif Central, France
p: Ancient; Salers produced for at least 2,000 years
d: Summer cheesemaking in stone mountain huts (burons) from pasture milk, producing large pressed tommes such as Salers and Laguiole.
tech: Raw milk renneted in a wooden gerle, curd pressed uncooked in large moulds, cave-matured
mat: Raw Salers, Aubrac or Simmental cows' milk
auth: PDO name on the rind; Salers only farmhouse-made between 15 April and 15 November; Laguiole bears a bull stamp and aluminium plaque.

d: Pastoral method of ripening salted, crumbled curd packed into a cleaned animal skin stored in caves or cellars.
tech: Curd drained, brined, kneaded with raw milk and packed tightly into a salted skin, then cellar-ripened for months
mat: Goat's or sheep's milk; goat, sheep or calf skin
auth: Ripened in real skin rather than plastic barrels; regional geographical-indication names such as Erzincan tulum.

r: Mongolia, Central Asia and the Caucasus
p: Nomadic pastoral tradition; dried yoghurt recorded in Arabic cookbooks from the 10th century
d: Pastoral dairy foods (tsagaan idee) eaten fresh in summer and dried into curd and yoghurt balls for winter.
tech: Churning yoghurt to remove butter, boiling and draining buttermilk curd, shaping and sun-drying for weeks
mat: Cow, yak, sheep, goat or mare's milk; salt
auth: Sun-dried, hand-shaped pieces with texture varying by animal; traditional qurut made from churned buttermilk rather than oven-fermented yoghurt.

r: Nepal, Bhutan, Tibet and Northeast India
d: Mountain cheesemaking from yak and cow buttermilk, producing soft fresh chhurpi and fire-dried hard chewing cheese.
tech: Buttermilk boiled, curd drained in cloth, pressed in jute bags, cut into cubes and dried over a fire
auth: Hard chhurpi is extremely hard and lasts 30 minutes to five hours in the mouth; soft chhurpi is white and mild.

p: Han dynasty onward; popular from the Song dynasty (960–1279)
d: Making bean curd by coagulating soy milk and pressing the curds, credited by legend to Prince Liu An.
tech: grinding soaked soybeans, boiling, coagulating with gypsum or bittern, pressing; fermenting and drying

d: Japanese tofu styles from silken kinugoshi and pressed momen to fried, frozen and freeze-dried forms.
tech: gypsum-set unpressed (kinugoshi) or pressed (momen) curd; deep-frying; freezing and freeze-drying

d: Fermenting soybeans with Rhizopus mould into a bound cake; said to have begun in Bayat, Klaten, Central Java. Indonesia submitted it to UNESCO's intangible heritage list in March 2024 (pending).
tech: soaking, dehulling and boiling beans, inoculating with Rhizopus and incubating in leaves or plastic
mat: soybeans, Rhizopus oligosporus or R. oryzae, teak or waru leaves

d: Grafted orchards of named local dessert and culinary apples, kept alive in estates, walled gardens and community orchards.
tech: grafting onto rootstocks; standard and espalier training
mat: apple, pear, plum, cherry, damson trees
ctr: English Heritage orchards at Walmer Castle, Mount Grace Priory, Barnard Castle, Osborne
auth: Named cultivars propagated by grafting, not seed

d: Mango cultivation and ritual in South Asia, with groves valued by Ashoka, the Mughals and in worship.
tech: grafting of monoembryonic cultivars such as Alphonso and Langra
auth: Named grafted cultivars; GI marks for several

d: Community-conserved native potato landraces, kept in Peru's Potato Park near Cusco with the International Potato Center.
tech: community seed conservation
ctr: Potato Park (Parque de la Papa), Sacred Valley
auth: grown by the six Quechua communities of the Potato Park

p: pre-Meiji (before 1868); name adopted 1960; brand certification from 1989
d: Heirloom vegetables of Kyoto, certified as brand products and tied to kaiseki and temple cooking.
tech: local seed selection, small-lot farming
auth: Kyoto Prefecture brand-product certification

d: Dry pasta made in Gragnano from durum semolina and Lattari mountain water.
tech: bronze-die extrusion, slow drying at 40-80 C
auth: IGP mark; produced and packed in Gragnano

d: Yuasa claims to be the birthplace of Japanese soy sauce, with a soy sauce industry flourishing since the Edo period.
tech: koji fermentation of soybean and wheat with brine, pressed and aged
auth: Claim of origin is local and not settled

d: Natural brewing of soy sauce in handmade cedar-and-bamboo kioke barrels, about 1% of Japan's soy sauce.
tech: Tennen Jōzō Kioke Shikomi: natural wooden-barrel fermentation
mat: cedar and bamboo barrels, soybean, wheat, salt
auth: Brewed in kioke barrels; barrels can last over 100 years

d: Making, keeping and eating jang, the fermented sauces including soybean paste, soy sauce and red chilli paste.
tech: meju bricks fermented, brine drawn as ganjang, remainder mashed as doenjang
auth: Family transmission, mother to daughter, in earthenware jars

d: Making and sharing kimchi for winter over about a month from the tenth lunar month, inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.
tech: salting and fermenting vegetables, once in earthenware jars buried in the ground
auth: Practice inscribed, not kimchi itself; North Korea's tradition inscribed separately in 2015

d: Partly oxidised cliff-grown tea from the Wuyi Mountains, made by withering, shaking, rolling, firing and baking.
tech: withering, making (shaking and rolling), stir-frying, kneading, baking
mat: Wuyi cultivars (Da Hong Pao, Rou Gui, Shui Xian, Tie Luo Han, Bai Jiguan)
auth: Mother-tree Da Hong Pao is rare; most market tea is from cuttings

d: Yunnan large-leaf tea compressed and aged, in raw (sheng) and wet-piled ripe (shou) styles.
tech: sun-drying, compression, natural ageing or wet piling (since 1973)
auth: Four-digit factory recipe numbers; 2008 standard limits the name to Yunnan tea

p: Tea planted from the late 12th century; sencha 1738
d: Japanese shaded and steamed green tea from Uji and neighbouring Kyoto areas.
tech: ōishita shading with straw or reed covers; steaming, rolling, kneading
auth: A regional name needs all-local leaf; many farmers still hand-process

r: Darjeeling and Kalimpong, West Bengal, India
d: Himalayan black tea famed for muscatel flavour, sold by flush.
tech: long withering, rolling, oxidation on trays, firing
auth: India's first GI (2004); EU PGI 2011; Tea Board logo certification mark

d: Black tea grown largely on smallholdings through the Kenya Tea Development Agency and sold at the Mombasa auction.
tech: crush-tear-curl (CTC) processing, plus orthodox whole leaf
auth: Sold by auction lot and factory; no single certification mark named

d: Oolong grown above 1,000 m in Nantou and Chiayi, hand-harvested at low yield.
tech: hand harvest, tarp withering, bruising, oxidation over about 36-40 hours
auth: Sweet, milky, floral cup; the source names no certification

r: Turkey and the former Ottoman lands
d: Very fine coffee boiled unfiltered with grounds left in the cup; on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.
tech: brought to the boil up to three times in a cezve
mat: Medium-roast arabica, copper cezve, thin porcelain cups
auth: Fine powder grind, cezve, thick froth, water served first

d: Lightly roasted coffee boiled unfiltered with cardamom and served unsweetened in small cups; on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.
tech: roasting in a mihmas, pounding in a mihbaj, boiling without filtering
mat: Arabica, cardamom, sometimes cloves or saffron
auth: Dallah pot, finjan cups, three cups poured partway

d: Household ritual of roasting, grinding and brewing coffee in a clay jebena for three rounds.
tech: pan roasting, mukecha grinding, jebena boiling, three rounds (abol, tona, baraka)
mat: Green coffee, clay jebena, handleless cups, incense
auth: Jebena pot, three rounds, hosted by the woman of the household

d: Brewing method using small pots and many short infusions of a large leaf quantity.
tech: short infusions of 10-15 seconds lengthening each pour
mat: Yixing clay teapot or gaiwan, thin porcelain cups, fairness cup
auth: Small vessels, repeated infusions, rinsing of pot and leaf

r: Maghreb: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Mauritania
d: Gunpowder green tea brewed with fresh spearmint and sugar, poured from a height.
tech: boiling water, leaves left in the pot, high pour
auth: Served at least three glasses; flavour changes glass to glass

d: Fermenting and ageing wine with skins, stalks and pips in large buried egg-shaped clay jars.
tech: whole-grape fermentation in sealed buried qvevri for 5–6 months or more; vessels lime-washed and beeswaxed
auth: label names qvevri/kvevri; long skin contact gives amber colour and tannin in whites

d: Botrytised aszú berries macerated in must and cask-aged; vineyards classified from 1730 in one of the first appellations.
tech: Hand-picking aszú berries, paste maceration, cask ageing; puttonyos grading
auth: Tokaji designation; puttonyos and vintage on label

p: Named in the 12th century; earlier roots
d: Sun-dried-grape dessert wine from 14 villages in the Troödos foothills, protected by Cypriot law of 1990 and EU PDO.
tech: Sun-drying grapes 7–10 days before pressing
auth: Commandaria PDO

p: more than a century (style after Märzen)
d: Bamberg brewers' tradition of lager brewed from malt kilned over open beechwood fires.
tech: Malt dried over beechwood log fires; beer lagered in cool cellars
auth: Brewed in Bamberg with in-house fire-kilned malt rather than industrial smoked malt; Slow Food Ark of Taste listing (2017).

d: Top-fermented, cold-conditioned pale ale brewed only within 50 km of Cologne under the Kölsch-Konvention.
tech: warm top fermentation then cold conditioning
mat: pale malt, some wheat allowed, hops
auth: Brewed by a Konvention signatory within 50 km of Cologne; served in the Stange.

d: Copper top-fermented ale brewed and poured in Düsseldorf's old-town house breweries.
tech: top fermentation, cold conditioning
auth: House alt drawn on the premises in the Altstadt; Sticke released on set days.

r: Belgium, Netherlands, Italy, England (formerly Austria, United States)
p: Monastic brewing since 1836 (Westmalle); ITA label from 1997
d: Label of the International Trappist Association for beers and goods made at Trappist abbeys under monastic supervision.
tech: Brewed within the immediate surroundings of the abbey under the supervision of monks or nuns; profits go to the community and charity
mat: Barley malt, hops, sugar, abbey yeast strains
auth: Hexagonal 'Authentic Trappist Product' logo on the label; 'abbey beer' or licensed brands such as Leffe or St. Bernardus are not Trappist.

r: Pajottenland and Senne valley, south-west of Brussels (Belgium)
p: 13th century to present; gueuze EU TSG 1997/98
d: Spontaneously fermented wheat beer, aged in wood and blended into gueuze or refermented on fruit, guarded by the High Council for Artisanal Lambic Beers (HORAL).
tech: Wort cooled overnight in an open coolship, inoculated by airborne yeasts and bacteria, brewed October to May, aged in barrels with old dry hops, blended young with old
mat: Barley malt, unmalted wheat, aged hops, oak barrels, whole fruit (Schaarbeek cherries, raspberries)
auth: 'Oude Gueuze'/'Oude Geuze' and 'Oude Kriek' on the label mean unsweetened blends of 100% lambic; HORAL contested 'Méthode Gueuze' abroad (Jester King now uses 'Méthode Traditionnelle').

d: Home brewing of maize and sorghum beer for initiation homecomings, weddings, funerals and calling the ancestors.
tech: Mash of maize meal and maize and sorghum malt fermented overnight in a potjie, strained, sediment returned
mat: Maize meal, maize malt, sorghum malt, water
auth: Thick, sour, opaque buff-coloured brew under 3% alcohol, made in a cast-iron pot.

d: Brewing of malted-maize beer, taught to women in the Inca aqlla wasi and used in feasts, alliances and rites.
tech: Germinated maize milled, boiled and fermented for days, then sieved through cloth
auth: Brewed from jora maize and served from clay chomba, wooden qero or gourd poto.

p: Farmhouse tradition to present; EU TSG
d: Farmhouse brewing of unboiled barley and rye ale lautered through juniper in a kuurna.
tech: Long step mash, lautering through juniper twigs, no boil, top fermentation with baking yeast
auth: Cloudy, barely carbonated, banana and juniper notes; TSG rules on process and ingredients.

r: Rwanda, Burundi, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, DR Congo
d: Fermenting juice of East African Highland bananas with roasted sorghum or millet for rituals and ceremonies.
tech: Ripe bananas juiced and diluted, mixed with ground roasted sorghum and fermented
mat: Highland bananas (igikashi, igisahira), sorghum, millet or maize flour
auth: Made from Highland cooking-type bananas with grain, low alcohol, unbottled.

d: Limbu drink of fermented finger millet served to honour guests and shared by newlyweds under the Mundhum.
tech: Cooked millet fermented with marchā starter, steeped in hot water, sipped through a filtering bamboo straw
mat: Finger millet, marchā, bamboo, wood or brass vessel
auth: Served as moist fermented millet in a tongba vessel topped up with hot water.

d: Artisan cane spirit made by some 500–600 village micro-distilleries (guildives).
tech: Spontaneous fermentation of cane juice or syrup; distillation in Creole stills; no filtration
auth: HaïRum certification mark

d: Spirit distilled from fermented sap of unopened coconut flowers.
tech: Sap tapping, fermentation, distillation; ageing in halmilla wood vats
auth: Only coconut sap and water in premium grades; common grades blended with molasses or neutral spirit

r: Valles region, Jalisco, Mexico (Tequila, Amatitán, El Arenal, Magdalena)
d: Blue-agave cultivation and tequila distilling, recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2006.
tech: Cooking, fermenting and distilling blue agave hearts
auth: NOM distillery number and Tequila Regulatory Council certification; '100% agave' on the label

r: Oaxaca and other DO states, Mexico
d: Village palenque mezcal making from cultivated and wild agaves.
tech: Pit-roasting agave, milling by mallet or stone tahona, fermenting, distilling in copper, clay or wood stills
mat: Agave (espadín, tobalá and other wild species)
auth: Certified category on label (mezcal, artesanal, ancestral), agave species and producer named

d: Hungarian fruit brandy distilled only from Hungarian-grown fruit, protected in the EU since 2004 and by the 2008 pálinka law.
tech: Whole-fruit mash fermentation; double distillation in small copper pot stills (kisüsti) or single column distillation
mat: Plums, apricots, apples, pears, cherries, sour cherries, quince, grape pomace
auth: Hungarian fruit and production, no additives beyond fruit, at least 37.5% ABV, registered distillery; regional PDO name where claimed.

d: Damson plum brandy; Serbia’s traditional šljivovica-making was inscribed on UNESCO’s intangible heritage list in 2022.
tech: Fermentation of lightly pressed plums with kernels intact; one or more distillations; often oak-aged
auth: Protected national names (Srpska šljivovica, Troyanska slivova, Tetevenska slivova); damson plum base.

d: Birthplace of commercial absinthe: Dubied and Pernod at Couvet, then Pernod Fils at Pontarlier; revived at Môtiers after legalisation.
tech: Maceration of wormwood, anise and fennel in alcohol, redistilled; verte gets a second herbal maceration for colour
mat: Grand wormwood, green anise, fennel, wine or neutral alcohol
auth: Swiss court ruled in 2014 that 'absinthe' is a product name, not a protected origin; look for named Val-de-Travers or Pontarlier distilleries.

d: Grape-and-aniseed spirit of the Levant, centred on Zahlé and the Bekaa Valley.
tech: Grapes fermented about three weeks, distilled, redistilled with aniseed, then a slow third distillation; aged in clay amphorae
auth: Quality arak is triple distilled and amphora-aged, typically about 53% ABV.

d: Okinawan rice spirit distilled with indigenous black koji and aged as kusu in clay pots; UNESCO-listed in 2024 among Japan's traditional koji knowledge.
tech: Single fermentation of steamed long-grain rice fully converted with black koji, single pot distillation, long ageing in clay pots
mat: Thai indica or Okinawan rice, black koji (Aspergillus luchuensis), clay pots
auth: 'Ryukyu Awamori' GI label (since 2004); age claim for kusu means at least the stated years

d: Traditional distilled rice soju of Andong, tied to the Yuan-era supply base and recorded in the 17th-century Ŭmsik timibang.
tech: Brewing a grain mash and distilling it in a soju gori still

p: Traditional; Ordine del Nocino Modenese since 1978
d: Walnut liqueur of green walnuts steeped in spirit and sweetened, a household and artisan tradition around Modena.
tech: Unripe walnuts picked around St John's Day (24 June), steeped in alcohol, mixed with syrup and aged
auth: Dark brown colour; traditional harvest around 24 June

p: from 1330; rise from the Kan'ei period (17th century)
d: Five brewing districts producing about a quarter of Japan's sake, known for strong, full sake.
tech: Tanba tōji brewmasters; cold Rokkō oroshi winds slow fermentation
mat: Miyamizu hard water from Mount Rokkō; Yamada Nishiki rice
auth: Nada-Gogō geographical indication on the label

p: Three Kingdoms to present; revived after 1990s
d: Home and regional brewing of rice wines and spirits with nuruk starters, suppressed under colonial rule and grain laws.
tech: Multi-stage fermentation of steamed rice with nuruk; clear cheongju drawn off, cloudy takju kept unfiltered
mat: Rice, glutinous rice, wheat nuruk, water, flowers and herbs
auth: Designated intangible-heritage recipes (e.g. No. 86-2, 86-3); traditional nuruk rather than manufactured starter

p: Ancient; spread nationally in the late Qing
d: Glutinous-rice huangjiu brewing with wheat qu, aged in earthenware jars and dated by brewing year.
tech: Fermentation with wheat-based qu; jar ageing for years or decades
mat: Glutinous rice, wheat qu, local water
auth: Wine from outside Shaoxing labelled as Shaoxing is a common fraud

d: The making, pouring and shared drinking of natural cider in Asturias, inscribed by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage in 2024.
tech: Natural fermentation of Asturian apples in cider mills; pouring from a height to aerate
auth: 100% Asturian apples; DOP Sidra de Asturias label

d: Sagardotegi cider houses where still cider is drawn straight from the barrel at the call of txotx during the season from 19 January.
tech: Double fermentation and maturing in oak or chestnut barrels

p: Medieval–present; grade names 17th–18th c.; EU TSG 2008
d: Mead made in four legally defined grades by honey-to-water ratio and ageing.
tech: Honey must fermented and aged 9 months to 3 years
mat: Honey, water, sometimes fruit juice or spices
auth: TSG label with grade name; ratio and minimum ageing per grade

d: Honey wine flavoured with gesho, made at home and sold in tej houses.
tech: Honey water fermented with boiled gesho stems and leaves, stirred daily, filtered
auth: Cloudy yellow, sweet, slightly effervescent; served in a berele

d: Fermented maguey sap drink sold in pulquerías.
tech: Aguamiel tapped twice daily and fermented 7–14 days with seed pulque (Zymomonas mobilis)
auth: Fresh, viscous, milky; canning changes the flavour

r: West Africa, South and Southeast Asia, Pacific, western Mexico
d: Tapping palm flower stalks for sap that ferments naturally within hours.
tech: Flower stalk cut and sap collected in a fastened container; wild-yeast fermentation
mat: Coconut, palmyra, oil, raffia, date, nipa or kaong palm sap
auth: Sold fresh; sours within a day

d: French artisan know-how and culture of baguette bread, on the UNESCO intangible heritage lists since 2022.
tech: Hand-shaped long loaves; tradition dough of flour, water, yeast and salt only (Décret Pain 1993)
auth: Sold as "baguette de tradition" only if made without additives or pre-made dough

r: Armenia, Iran, Azerbaijan, Turkey, Central Asia
d: Thin flatbread slapped on the walls of a tonir clay oven; UNESCO-listed for Armenia (2014) and multinationally (2016).
tech: Dough stretched thin and baked 15–40 seconds on tonir walls

d: Christmas fruit stollen baked by Dresden bakers.
tech: yeast dough with macerated fruit, sugared
mat: butter, dried and candied fruit, almonds
auth: seal showing Augustus the Strong

d: Guild-baked honey-spice cakes, protected since 1996.
tech: nut-rich dough baked on wafer
auth: made within the city; Elisen grade ≥25% nuts, <10% flour

d: Hard Lebkuchen from Aachen with protected origin.
tech: baked spiced dough
auth: maker located in or near Aachen (PGI)

d: Traditional Polish gingerbread of Toruń.
tech: moulded spiced honey dough

d: Portuguese-derived sponge cake regarded as wagashi.
tech: baked in square moulds with mizuame and zarame

d: Syrup waffles first baked in Gouda and still made there by bakeries and factories.
tech: thin waffle baked on an iron, split and filled with syrup

d: Twice-baked almond biscuits of Prato following Antonio Mattei's recipe.
tech: baked as a log, sliced and baked again

d: Caramelised or spiced biscuits of the Low Countries, listed in Brussels' intangible heritage inventory in 2020.
tech: moulded or cut biscuit

d: Rye hard bread baked in thin rounds with a central hole and dried on poles.
tech: thin-rolled rye dough baked dry, often sourdough
auth: Rye-based, very low moisture, traditional round form with hole.

d: Turin breadsticks in the hand-rolled rubatà and stretched stirato forms.
tech: hand-rolling (rubatà) or stretching (stirato)
mat: wheat flour, water, yeast, olive oil
auth: Rubatà show an irregular knobby hand-rolled surface and run 40–80 cm.

d: Sicilian cold-worked chocolate brought under Spanish rule, kept grainy because the sugar never dissolves.
tech: worked "a freddo" below 40 °C, not conched; once rolled on lava stone, poured into pewter moulds as thick bars
mat: cocoa with its butter, sugar; optional cinnamon, vanilla, ginger, chilli, almonds, citrus peel
ctr: Consorzio di Tutela del Cioccolato di Modica (2003)
auth: PGI mark; grainy rough texture, small air bubbles, crumbly break, slightly grey bloom; no milk, vegetable fat or lecithin

d: Turin chocolate-making that blends chocolate with hazelnut paste, giving the gianduiotto and cremino.
tech: chocolate blended with about 30% hazelnut paste
auth: ingot shape and hazelnut share

r: United Kingdom and Ireland (also Denmark, Australia)
d: Lettered peppermint sticks of boiled sugar made and sold at seaside resorts.
tech: letters built from strips of coloured sugar, assembled in spelling order, then the block stretched thin
mat: boiled sugar, peppermint or spearmint flavouring, colourings
auth: lettering runs through the whole stick; made on site at the resort

d: Liquorice discs from a town where liquorice was grown, stamped with the castle.
tech: liquorice paste sweetened and stamped into small discs
auth: small black discs about 19 mm across with a castle stamp

d: Liquorice flavoured with ammonium chloride (salmiak), from mild to double salt.
tech: liquorice mass flavoured or dusted with salmiak salt
mat: liquorice extract, ammonium chloride, sugar, starch
auth: salmiak listed in ingredients; dubbelzout marks double salt

d: Starch-and-sugar gel confection of Ottoman tradition.
tech: starch and sugar cooked to a gel, set, cut into cubes and dusted
auth: Loukoumi Geroskipou carries the Cyprus PGI

r: Balkans, Middle East, Central and South Asia
d: Seed-paste and flour-based halvas made across a wide region.
tech: seed paste or roasted flour cooked with sugar and fat; floss types pulled
mat: sesame tahini, sunflower seed, flour, sugar, ghee

d: Christmas almond-and-honey turrón of Jijona, Alicante and Agramunt.
tech: almonds with honey, sugar and egg white, ground to paste (Jijona) or left whole (Alicante)
auth: PGI labels; about 64% almonds (Jijona) and 60% (Alicante)

d: Regional Italian nougats eaten at Christmas.
tech: egg white, sugar and honey whipped and set with nuts
auth: Torrone di Bagnara holds the Italian IGP

d: White honey-and-almond nougat of Montélimar.
tech: whipped egg white with lavender honey and sugar, set with roasted nuts
mat: lavender honey, almonds, pistachios, egg white
auth: protected status since 2024

d: Persian nougat traditionally made with psyllid manna from Zagros shrubs.
tech: egg white and manna or sugar beaten with nuts and rosewater
mat: psyllid manna, egg white, pistachios, almonds, rosewater
auth: traditional gaz uses manna rather than sugar and corn syrup

d: High-almond marzipan of the former Hanseatic hub.
tech: almond paste worked with limited sugar and moulded or coated
auth: PGI since 1996: at most 30% sugar, Fine at most 10%

d: Toledo marzipan with protected status.
tech: almonds and sugar kneaded and shaped
auth: PGI: almonds at least 50% by weight

d: Seasonal Japanese confectionery served with green tea.
tech: bean paste, rice and agar cooked, moulded or steamed; graded by moisture
mat: azuki, rice, mochi, agar, wasanbon sugar

d: Milk, flour and nut sweets made by halwai shops for festivals and gifts.
tech: milk reduced to khoya or curdled to chhena, flour roasted in ghee, sugar syrup
mat: milk, chhena, gram flour, ghee, nuts, silver leaf
auth: GI tags: Banglar Rasogolla (2017), Odisha Rasagola (2019)

d: Sugared almonds of Sulmona, used as favours and arrangements.
tech: almonds panned in layers of sugar
auth: listed as a prodotto agroalimentare tradizionale (PAT)

d: Melon-and-almond calissons made mostly in Aix.
tech: candied melon and orange ground with almonds, iced and cut to an almond shape
mat: candied melon, orange, almonds, royal icing
auth: name protected in France since 1991

d: Candied chestnuts made by a near twenty-step process.
tech: chestnuts candied in syrup over days and glazed, much by hand

d: Pistachio baklava of Gaziantep, recipe brought from Damascus.
tech: thin filo layers with pistachio, baked and soaked in syrup
auth: Turkish GI 2008; EU PGI 2013

d: Industrial and artisan alfajores filled with dulce de leche.
tech: biscuits sandwiched with dulce de leche, coated in chocolate or sugar
mat: flour or cornstarch, dulce de leche, chocolate

d: Crisp spiced noodle snack made as a cottage industry around Bikaner.
tech: dough of moth-bean and gram flour with spices pressed into fine strands and deep-fried
mat: Vigna aconitifolia (moth bean), gram flour, spices
auth: light yellow, crunchier and more strongly flavoured than sev; made in Bikaner

d: Salty soy-glazed rice crackers popularised from a Sōka teahouse.
tech: rice crackers baked and brushed with soy sauce

d: Knotted soft pretzels dipped in lye before baking.
tech: dough twisted into the pretzel loop, dipped in lye or washing soda, salted and baked
auth: Bavarian: thick arms, little fat; Swabian: thin arms, split fat belly

d: Artisanal Italian ice cream tradition of low-fat, low-air gelato made daily in gelaterie.
tech: custard or milk base pasteurised, batch-frozen with little air
auth: 6–9% butterfat, 20–35% air, served softer than ice cream

d: Unchurned frozen dessert of slow-reduced milk, sold by kulfiwallahs.
tech: milk reduced and caramelised, frozen in sealed moulds in a matka of ice and salt
ctr: Kuremal Mohan Lal Kulfi Wale, Old Delhi (1906)
auth: dense, slow-melting, no ice crystals, cooked-milk taste

d: Fresh-fruit ice pops, milk- or water-based, made by paleterías and sold by paleteros.
tech: fresh fruit frozen on a stick
auth: fresh-fruit base; local flavours such as tamarind, mamey, horchata

d: Turkish mastic ice cream thickened with salep.
tech: pounded and stretched rather than churned
auth: chewy, elastic, slow to melt

r: Iran, Turkey, Arab world, South Asia
p: Medieval Persian origin; Mughal India from 16th century
d: Sweet fruit, flower and herb syrups diluted with water, popular at Ramadan iftar.
tech: Fruit juice, petals or essences boiled with sugar into syrup; Ottoman crystallised tablets
mat: rose, sandalwood, bael, khus, lemon, pomegranate, tamarind, sugar

d: Fruit infused in vinegar, sweetened and reduced to a syrup for mixing with water or soda.
tech: Vinegar infusion of fruit, strained, sweetened and reduced

p: first recorded 988; commercial from the late 19th century
d: Low-alcohol rye bread or malt drink brewed at home and sold from street barrels and bottles.
tech: rye bread or malt soaked in hot water, short fermentation with yeast and lactic bacteria
mat: rye bread, rye malt, sugar, yeast, berries or herbs
auth: fermented from bread or malt, under about 1.2–1.5% alcohol; unfermented malt-extract drinks are kvass-style beverages

p: recorded in the 11th century; golden age under the Ottomans
d: Thick fermented grain drink sold by boza makers and street vendors in winter.
tech: ground cereal fermented and kept cool
auth: thick, tart, about 1% alcohol; served cold in winter

d: Quick street-vendor ferment of pineapple peel, once made from maize.
tech: wild fermentation of peel with sugar for one to two days, sometimes in barrels
mat: pineapple peel and rind, piloncillo, cinnamon, chilli
auth: slight fizz and tartness from live fermentation; sold chilled

p: traditional; now mostly a soft drink
d: Bittersweet bark drink, once fermented in small batches, now often syrup or soda.
tech: bark and spices boiled, bottled and sun-warmed, fermented up to a week with a previous batch
mat: Colubrina bark, cinnamon, cloves, aniseed, orange peel, brown sugar
auth: bitter bark taste; fermented versions foam

d: Strong 'silk-stocking' black tea with evaporated milk, sold fresh and as cold milk tea in cans and bottles.
tech: Ceylon black tea blend mixed with evaporated or condensed milk
forms: canned or bottled cold milk tea
auth: smooth, strong tea with evaporated milk; technique listed as Hong Kong intangible cultural heritage (2017)
